title: एउटा सल्लाह कवितामा पौरस्त्य दर्शन {Paurastya philosophy in an advice poem}
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेखमा शिवगोपाल रिसालद्वारा रचिएको एउटा सल्लाह कवितालाई पौरस्त्य दर्शनका कोणबाट विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । आध्यात्मिक विषयलाई सांसरिक जीवनसँग तादात्म्य गराएर यसलाई अपरिहार्य ठानी अगाडि बढाउने कवि रिसालको उक्त कवितामा पौरस्त्य दर्शनको प्रस्तुति भएको छ । यस कवितामा मूलतः मनलाई अध्यात्ममा वा ईश्वरमा लगाउँर मोक्ष प्राप्त गर्नुपर्ने चिन्तनलाई प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । ईश्वरको अस्तित्वलाई स्वीकार्ने आस्तिक वेदान्त दर्शनको मूल मर्म यस कवितामा आएको छ । मनको शुद्धता, ईश्वरको चिन्तन, जीवनको क्षणिकता, भौतिक वस्तुप्रति वितृष्णा, मनको चिन्तनजस्ता विषयमा केन्द्रित रहे पनि कवितामा मूलतः आत्मज्ञानको अर्थात् मोक्ष प्राप्तिको ध्येय राखिएको छ । हरेक मानिसलाई सांसरिक विषय वासनाले मोक्ष प्राप्तिमा वाधा गरिरहेको हुन्छ । त्यो वासनालाई हटाएर आÇनो स्वरूप आत्मा प्राप्ति गर्नु नै प्रस्तुत कविताको दार्शनिक चिन्तन रहेको निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: In the present article, the poem "Euta Salla" (An Advice), composed by Shivagopal Risal, is analyzed from the perspective of Eastern philosophy. In this poem by poet Risal—who harmonizes spiritual matters with worldly life and advances them as indispensable—Eastern philosophy is presented. In this poem, the thought is primarily presented that one must attain liberation (moksha) by focusing the mind on spirituality or God. The core essence of theistic Vedanta philosophy, which acknowledges the existence of God, is incorporated into this poem. Although focused on themes such as purity of mind, contemplation of God, the transience of life, aversion to material objects, and reflection of the mind, the poem is essentially aimed at self-knowledge, that is, the attainment of liberation. For every human being, worldly desires and passions impede the attainment of liberation. The conclusion drawn is that eliminating those passions and realizing the true nature of one's own soul constitutes the philosophical thinking of the present poem.

informal_english: In this paper, Shivagopal Risal's poem "Euta Salla" (A Bit of Advice) gets looked at through the lens of Eastern philosophy. Poet Risal ties spiritual stuff right into everyday worldly life and treats it as an absolute must, and that Eastern philosophy shines straight through his poem. The poem's main thrust is that you've gotta turn your mind towards spirituality or God to reach moksha. The heart of theistic Vedanta philosophy, which accepts that God actually exists, comes right through in the poem. Even though it focuses on things like keeping a pure mind, thinking about God, life being short, ditching interest in material stuff, and sorting out your thoughts, the main goal is still self-knowledge—that is, reaching liberation. In every one of us, worldly cravings end up blocking the road to liberation. The takeaway is that shedding those cravings and discovering your true inner self, the soul, is what the poem's philosophy is all about.
